A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-J. Matching the content across pagination changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original OpenWebText training experiments, categorical-sampling ablations, and generation-quality and runtime comparisons (Table 2, Figure 9, Appendix J).

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including the precision ablation, training comparisons, and evaluations of first-hitting sampling.

M1.justification: The training formulations, first-hitting sampler and its parallel and high-order variants, and categorical-sampling correction are unchanged (Sections 3-6; Algorithms 1-4). The added attention discussion introduces no implemented component.

E1.justification: OpenWebText training, validation, and text-generation coverage is unchanged. The new discussion of long-context LLM deployment adds no evaluated scenario; the DiffSound efficiency example already appears in v4 Appendix J.3.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain AR, SEDD Absorb, and MDLM, including MDLM with and without caching (Figures 7 and 9). The newly cited attention-acceleration methods are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix H retains the same data split and preprocessing, 1024-token sequences, model configurations, training budgets, and evaluation metrics. Sampling-step sweeps, precision settings, and temperature experiments also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The precision/truncation ablation, training-variant and variance-reduction studies, high-order sampler comparisons, efficiency analysis, and generated-text cases are retained unchanged (Table 2; Appendix J). No new robustness or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: The reported averaging over 64 generated samples and the eight-sample precision ablation are unchanged (Appendix H.4; Section 5.2). Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 retains the same Gen PPL/entropy pairs: 31.24/5.17 for 32-bit, 126.11/5.66 for 64-bit, and 28.64/5.12 for truncated 64-bit sampling. Corresponding plots, reported trends, efficiency examples, and generated texts also match.

T1.justification: Propositions 3.1, 3.2, 4.1, and 5.2 and their Appendix C proofs are unchanged. The definitions and additional derivations in the appendices are also retained; equation relocation does not alter their mathematical content.

C1.justification: v6 adds an introduction-level claim that KV-caching limitations undermine MDMs' prospects for replacing ARMs at LLM scale. The central equivalence, sampler-speedup, and numerical-bias contributions remain. Removing the final limitations paragraph also drops v4's explicit speculation about the entire discrete-diffusion family.

C2.justification: v6 introduces a bidirectional-attention/KV-caching explanation for deployment inefficiency and identifies quantized or sparse attention as outside its scope. It removes the explicit statement that the work does not substantially improve architectures or training. The conclusion's text-order caveat and possible applicability to order-agnostic data remain.

D1.justification: Algorithms, implementation choices, hyperparameters, hardware, training time, preprocessing, and pretrained-model access information in Appendices G-H are unchanged. Renumbering the MDLM repository footnote does not change access information.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds SageAttention, SageAttention2, and SpargeAttn as infrastructure approaches to inference acceleration outside this work's scope. The introduction also newly criticizes prior diffusion-language-model work for overlooking or downplaying KV-caching limitations; the existing novelty positioning otherwise remains.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: the introduction expands its criticism and clarifies the temperature/perplexity mechanism, a footnote and acknowledgments are added, and the concluding limitations paragraph is removed. The overall section and appendix organization remains stable.

P2.justification: Text reflow changes figure, equation, and table placement; Table 2 moves from PDF page 8 to page 9. The same figures and tables remain with unchanged substantive displays, alongside minor typography and bibliography-layout changes.

improvement.justification: v6 adds useful infrastructure context, but its new allegation that most prior work overlooked or intentionally downplayed KV-caching limitations is not substantiated in the paper. It also extends deployment conclusions without new scaling evidence. These additions modestly weaken the grounding of the discussion, while the unchanged methods, proofs, experiments, and retained text-order caveat preserve the main scientific contribution.
